headline: On last trading day, Sensex and Nifty snapped two-week gains as rising crude oil prices weighed on markets.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 26 October.

why: Surging crude oil prices hitting six-month highs dragged Indian equities to weekly losses.
Macro uncertainty and rising global oil prices created strong selling pressure.
Investors engaged in profit-taking after the market snapped its two-week winning streak.
Sensex shed around 1,600 points during a highly turbulent trading week.
whatHappening: In the last trading session, Nifty ended at 22,600 while Sensex fell 125 points.
Bank of India announced that it has made no ECL provisions yet.
Shriram Finance aims to double down on gold loans despite repayment red flags.
Grey market indicators suggest over 22% listing gains for the upcoming Jio IPO.
summary: Indian markets ended lower in the last session, snapping a two-week winning streak as crude oil prices surged toward six-month highs. Sensex lost 125 points while Nifty closed around the 22,600 level amidst global macro headwinds. Stock-specific action was seen in financial names like Bank of India and Shriram Finance.
